transcript:
This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix in to your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to Kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Kievone.
Chip Giant Nvidia led a big stock market rally today after exiled president at CEO Jensen Wong was
reinstated to his leadership positions.
President Trump says he called on the tech giant to take Wong back despite his multiple affairs,
specifically one with a woman suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The entanglement raised concerns about national security
which President Trump has dismissed. The latest development led Wall Street to recover about half of last week's losses.
Nvidia's board brought back Wong less than two weeks after he resigned. Many Silicon Valley CEOs and investors are
welcoming his reinstatement and PR Shannon Bond has more. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk posted on social media, quote, "the mistake has been corrected."
Gavin Baker, whose firm Invest in NVIDIA, posted a video of employees cheering and clapping for Wong at the chipmaker's headquarters.
Tech historian Margaret O'Mara says the reaction reflects Silicon Valley's reverence for founders.
It's the argument made by a lot in Silicon Valley last week and by the president that
NVIDIA's success depends on Jensen running it. Many tech leaders have loudly called for Wong's return,
even as questions remain after the NVIDIA founder admitted to having an affair with a woman U.S.
officials suspected of working with Chinese intelligence. Shannon Bond, NPR News.
Congressman Jimmy Gomez says he's resigning from Congress. That's after a bipartisan investigation found substantial evidence that
California Democrat engaged in sexual misconduct toward a house staffer. NPR's Sam Gringles reports.
The House Ethics Committee concluded his actions violated house rules by, quote, "making unwelcome sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome
sexual conduct towards a house staffer." The report also found the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.
Gomez lost reelection this fall and denied the encounters were non-consensual. In a statement, he wrote he has strong
disagreements with the report and its conclusions. The committee said Gomez's actions point to a broader culture of disrespect and
toxic sexual behavior toward staff that permeates life on the Hill and is long overdue for correction.
This year, two other house members have also resigned amid sexual misconduct allegations. And last week, the Ethics Committee unveiled new rules to help speed
investigations and improve transparency. Sam Gringles, NPR News, Washington.
A federal appeals court says it is okay for the Army to detonate several tons of degraded
balm-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant. President Trump had ordered the Army to wait for the courts to weigh in.
68 barrels of leaded materials are involved, and environmental activists objected to the introduction of lead pollutants in the atmosphere near
Middleton, Iowa. The Army has said there's a risk that cold weather will destabilize the explosive materials.
The Dow gained 1447 points today. The S&P up 326. This is NPR.
Gasoline prices in the U.S. continue falling as millions of Americans begin traveling for the Thanksgiving holiday.
Triple-A says regular is now averaging about
364 a gallon. That's a drop of roughly 65 cents over the last month amid fewer disruptions to oil tackers in the Middle East.
A compounding pharmacy is recalling a broad range of its peptide injections.
They may not be sterile, according to the Food and Drug Administration. And PR's Sydney Lufkin has details.
Greenwich RX is recalling peptides at dispense between August 10th and September 21st. The compounding pharmacy located in Tumbull,
Texas, dispensed peptides nationwide. The recalled peptides include BPC 157,
which is one the Trump administration loosened restrictions on late last month. The recall also includes compounded weight-loss medicines containing the same active
ingredients as Wagovae and Zepbound. According to Greenwich RX, the sterility concerns arose after an FDA inspection.
The company says it hasn't found evidence of contamination, but it is initiating the recall as a precaution.
Injecting a product that is not sterile could have serious health consequences. A list of the recalled peptides is on FDA's website, Sydney Lufkin, NPR News.
Realtor.com says its latest study shows that more than 25 million young Americans between 18 and 34 live with their parents.
Most are under age 25. The numbers just below the peak experienced during the pandemic.
The report cites high home prices and mortgage rates pricing out many would-be first-time homebuyers.
I'm Louise Givoni, NPR News, Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
The app guides users to intuitively think in a second language using images and contextual audio,
mimicking how people acquire speech as children. The platform also includes advanced speech recognition
technology that compares a learner's pronunciation directly with native speakers to refine accent precision.
Learn more about their immersion method and the new Rosetta Stone Sapphire app at RosettaStone.com.

topics.text: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after resignation, sparking stock market rally
Congressman Jimmy Gomez resigns after House Ethics finds sexual misconduct toward staffer
Federal appeals court allows Army to detonate degraded explosive materials at Iowa ammunition plant
Gasoline prices continue falling as Thanksgiving travel begins, AAA reports average near $3.64
Greenwich Rx recalls peptide injections over possible sterility concerns, FDA says
Realtor.com study finds over 25 million young Americans living with parents
